title: look.set on a WordPress block theme beats a rule in global styles itself (a design-system slot's) strictly, since Additional CSS is printed before theme.json's own styles.css there
steps: S1: From packages/tools/tracy-site-tools run: node --test --test-reporter=tap test/look-set.test.mjs
S2: Read the test named in run.tests: look.set scope site for a token whose winning declaration stands in global-styles-inline-css, once on the slot's `:root`×6 selector and once on `:root`.
expect: The token set on `:root:root:root:root:root:root` is set again in Additional CSS on `:root:root:root:root:root:root:not(.\#)` (0,7,0), more specific than the slot's (0,6,0).
The token set on `:root` (theme.json's variables, printed before Additional CSS) is set again on `:root` alone, as before.
evidence: dskeepwp 10/10/2026, WordPress 7.1.3: a block theme's Additional CSS is merged into global-styles-inline-css after variables/styles/presets and before theme.json's styles.css, where tracy-ds-slot writes its :root×6 rules — a selector equally specific there loses by order (look.set answered LOOK_SET_NO_EFFECT).
fence: on a block theme, a winner in the same global-styles sheet more specific than :root is beaten strictly (beyond)

tests: 🔒 WordPress, a block theme: a token a design-system slot sets in global styles
